subsystems.name: GPU compute nodes
subsystems.role: the actual number-crunching — dense servers each holding several GPUs wired tightly together.

subsystems.name: Cluster interconnect
subsystems.role: lets tens of thousands of GPUs act as one machine during a training run.

subsystems.name: Liquid cooling
subsystems.role: removes heat directly from chips, which air alone cannot do at this density.
parts: cold plates on GPUs and CPUs
facility water loop and dry coolers or cooling towers

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: delivers hundreds of megawatts to racks without a voltage sag.
parts: busway or busbar to the row

subsystems.name: Storage and data pipeline
subsystems.role: feeds training data in fast enough and saves checkpoints before failures.

subsystems.name: Orchestration software
subsystems.role: schedules jobs, detects failed GPUs and restarts training from the last checkpoint.

buildSteps.title: Secure power and a site
buildSteps.detail: A cluster of this size needs hundreds of megawatts. Developers negotiate grid interconnection, and where the grid cannot deliver fast enough, install on-site gas turbines and battery storage.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the hall
buildSteps.detail: Existing or new buildings are fitted out with reinforced floors, overhead cable trays, fire suppression and space for water-cooling plant.

buildSteps.title: Install electrical and cooling plant
buildSteps.detail: Substations, transformers, busway, coolant distribution units and the external water loop are commissioned before any hardware arrives.

buildSteps.title: Rack and cable the nodes
buildSteps.detail: GPU servers are rolled in, connected to power and network, and their cold plates linked to the coolant manifolds with quick-disconnects that allow a server to be pulled without draining the loop.

buildSteps.title: Build the network fabric
buildSteps.detail: Tens of thousands of cables and optical links are dressed into a multi-tier topology, then tested link by link and end to end.

buildSteps.title: Load the software stack
buildSteps.detail: Drivers, communication libraries, the scheduler and monitoring are installed and version-locked across the whole cluster.

buildSteps.title: Burn in and benchmark
buildSteps.detail: Synthetic and collective tests — all-reduce and all-to-all — run for days to find weak links, thermally marginal racks and dead GPUs.

buildSteps.title: Hand over to training
buildSteps.detail: Production training jobs start, alongside continuous fault handling: at this scale, hardware failures are routine rather than exceptional.

prerequisites.why: training large models is limited by how fast GPUs can exchange gradients, not by raw compute alone.
racks drawing tens of kilowatts cannot be cooled by air alone.
grid connections of hundreds of megawatts take years to secure; on-site generation is a workaround.
frameworks and collective libraries must split a model across thousands of GPUs.
with failures every few hours, training must resume quickly rather than restart.

pathway.milestone: single-site clusters of roughly 100,000 GPUs, such as xAI's Colossus in Memphis brought online in 2024
pathway.unlocks: training runs that were previously impossible at any budget.

pathway.milestone: refresh to newer GPU generations and denser liquid-cooled racks at the same site
pathway.unlocks: more effective compute without a new grid connection.

pathway.milestone: multi-site clusters joined by long-haul optical links, presented as one logical machine
pathway.unlocks: scaling past what any single power grid can supply.

pathway.milestone: gigawatt campuses with high-voltage DC rack power and on-site generation
pathway.unlocks: frontier training at a scale that reshapes grid planning and siting rules.
